P1.evidence: Acknowledged the application without reading it back: 'I saw that you already wrote a few things down, but I would like to hear just everything from you.' The frame covered where you are, where you want to go and the fit test, but not what is in the way or what you need — 'see if it actually fits with Trevor. If it does, I'll take it through how, and otherwise I'll point you in the best direction.' Agreement asked and given ('Sounds good? Perfect'), and the open question ran: 'so tell me, like, what can we potentially help you out with, Alexandre?'

P2.evidence: Age was asked directly ('sorry, how old are you now?') but height and weight were volunteered inside his own weight-loss story, never requested. Injuries were done properly and with follow-up: 'do you have any injuries, things that we should know about?' produced the foot pain, the asymmetric shoulder and the weak wrists. Nutrition was excellent — a full day-in-the-life plus the client-dinner and evening-crash detail. Results from current training were established clearly. But occupation was never asked (the spirits industry and the travel both arrived unprompted), health conditions and heredity were never asked, the training week was confirmed back rather than elicited, and sleep and energy were never asked — eight hours a night surfaced only because he volunteered his supplement stack.

P3.evidence: The strongest goals work in the batch. Surface goals were pinned down and summarised back. The bridge ran well: 'why is it important for you to actually get to that next level, instead of just staying exactly where you are... there's so many 34 year olds with two kids who are like, I'm happy.' The feeling question ran and landed: 'when you can look in the mirror and see that, what sort of feeling would come up?' produced 'I would be proud of myself.' From there it drove through to family and legacy — the daughter who copies him, 'I would like to do at 50 some Hyrox with my daughter', and longevity. Not asked: a specific physical thing he cannot currently do, and an explicit 'who else does that impact'. The reflect-back was a goal summary rather than the scripted 'this isn't really about the weight' reframe.

P4.evidence: Asked what he had tried ('have you ever worked with a trainer before online?', plus the calisthenics programme and the ChatGPT-built plan), what happened with it, and why now. The prospect named the gap himself: 'I feel that maybe I've reached my point of getting the knowledge and maybe people that has the experience could help me.' The rep then ran the script's root-cause move in a modernised form: 'a lot of the times people have tried ChatGPT, Claude, every single model to get them a program, but they're always running against the same wall, and that's not having actual feedback' — which is the information-isn't-the-problem line adapted to this prospect, and it landed. Partial on why-it-didn't-stick only because his adherence never failed; the failure was in results, and the rep did not fully separate the two.

P5.evidence: The settle question ran and ran well: 'let's say life gets busy... are you just willing to let it drop, or are you not willing to settle for that reality?' — answered 'Oh, no. No, no, I really want to reach it.' But there was no two-year cost-of-inaction question, no 'why not', and no line in the sand. Worse, the rep later dismantled the frame himself during the money conversation: 'if we would have been in that state, you would have probably been like, yes, I need to do this because of your weight. That's not the case at the moment.' He told a hesitating prospect that the stakes were low.

P6.evidence: Run twice, before the offer and after it. At 00:27:53: 'when we do all of those things, do you feel like there would be any reason for you not to get to the results?' — which surfaced the real obstacle, his wife's snacking, and the rep converted it into a commitment ('are you willing to commit to that?' — 'Yes, that's something I start to do right now'). Repeated at 00:46:51 after the pillars: 'do you feel like there's anything else that would stop you?' — 'I don't think so.' A clear yes was in hand before price was named, which is exactly what the phase is for.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted three times and no payment was taken; the rep ended by deferring the link to the end of the month. Step 2 does not apply — the tier he was sold has no one-to-one onboarding call with Trevor. No agreement email and nothing signed. Skool was discussed and access confirmed as the mechanism ('then you give me, grant me access to the school area, right? Exactly') but nothing was actually set up, so step 4 is partial at best.

objection_plays.detail: Trigger at 00:50:40. Ran: a clean isolate ('is it more of a, I just don't have that available for myself, or is it more of a, if we do it, we just have to figure out how to actually do it?'), the worth test ('do you feel like that is worth the 5.2k for you?' — 'For me, yes'), cash-on-hand ('what do you have set aside for yourself?' — 1.5k) and a later split-payment probe. Not run: the should/how reframe, the open-honest-conversation permission ask, monthly surplus, credit cards, available credit, investments — the last of which mattered, because he volunteered 'I do kind of investments and stuff' and it was never followed. The play was abandoned mid-way and replaced by a cheaper product.

Trigger at 00:50:51, 'I share everything with my wife, need to discuss also with my wife'. Ran: the money-aside personal test, 'what do you think that her thoughts are going to be overall? What do you think that she would find nice about it?', and the ownership probe about him being the household money manager. Not run: 'is there any reason she would NOT want you stronger and less in pain', the 'this isn't a joint decision like buying a house' frame, and the deposit-with-refund fallback. He got the diagnosis and stopped before the close.

Trigger at 01:04:55, a policy-level 'I never say yes on the call.' The rep ran one move — 'what's stopping you from saying, yeah, let's get going, will call her afterwards?' — and then conceded the point entirely: 'I'm not going to force you to do anything... It sounds like you're serious. It's not like it's a getaway card.' None of the deciding-versus-thinking sequence ran. He converted the objection into a payment date instead of testing it.

Cashflow timing surfaced at 01:05:49 with the end-of-month paycheck. The rep ran one urgency move — 'half of the month is still half the month which you're sort of throwing away' — and one workaround, offering to split the $1,000 to start now. Nothing else from OD ran: no 'things never slow down', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', no 'the only thing you can control is right now'.

No fear or doubt trigger was raised, but the rep borrowed the OE plane move and repurposed it for the money objection: 'when they do the whole introduction of what to do when it goes wrong in the cabin... put your mask first' followed by 'do you feel like investing in yourself a little bit more than you usually would is a good thing?'. Worth noting as a play used out of its intended slot — it produced agreement in principle and no movement on the decision.

Script gap. This prospect's blocker was a competing capital allocation inside a household — a 20k car and a wife who had just taken a pay cut — not an inability to pay and not a lack of belief. There is no play for 'the money exists but it is already spoken for by the family', and the rep had nothing to reach for except a cheaper product.

notes: Discovery, goals and the commitment check were the best in this batch — he had a clear yes and a family-level why before he named a price. Then the money phase gave it all back: he undercut his own consequence frame ('that's not the case at the moment'), abandoned OC halfway, and cut the price from $6,000 to $1,000 to match a budget number the prospect had just said out loud. Coach the transition, not the discovery.
